title: Resilience Fund coverage is conditional on using counsel that satisfies the Lawyer Registry criteria
content:
The claim process begins not with the loss but with the lawyer. A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.1 requires the beneficiary to present counsel and a quote naming the lawyer, the firm, a PoE if not already in the registry, an initial payment to commence work, and a global fee estimate. A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.1.1 then fast-tracks the compliant case: if counsel is RF-qualified in the Lawyer Registry, "the claim is automatically submitted to the Claim Approval process."

If not, A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.1.2 sends the lawyer through acceptance criteria review, with two outcomes — pre-approval plus addition to the registry, or rejection, in which case "the Beneficiary must propose a different Legal Counsel."

The rationale is quality and cost control: a defendant under pressure is a poor negotiator, and an approved-panel model prevents the fund from underwriting whichever firm was reachable first. Requiring the quote upfront also gives Sky an exposure estimate before committing.

The cost is that the beneficiary's choice of counsel becomes Sky's decision. Someone facing a subpoena may already trust a specific lawyer with the relevant history and jurisdiction; if that lawyer fails registry criteria, the beneficiary must switch or self-fund. Combined with the absence of any acquired right, the person under legal threat controls neither whether they are funded nor by whom they are represented — and the registry gate applies before anyone has evaluated the merits of the loss.
